title: Upper Deck Seat Track in the Wet Bays — Detailed Corrosion Inspection
abstract: Repeat detailed inspection of the upper deck seat track and the beam flange beneath it in the bays under the galleys and the lavatories, where fluid running down the open track channel collects at the fastener line.

sections.purpose: This task gives the repeat detailed inspection of the upper deck seat track and the floor beam upper flange in the bays under the galleys and the lavatories, and the criteria for reporting a corrosion finding.
sections.job_setup_note: The inspection needs the carpet up, the seats out of the bay and the floor panels lifted. Plan it with a cabin task that already opens the floor. Have the depth gauge and the inspection mirror set available. The attack starts where fluid stands, so the lighting has to reach the bottom of the open track channel: use the channel lamp along the run rather than a hand lamp from above, which throws its own shadow into the channel.
sections.procedure: Remove the carpet, the seats and the floor panels from the bay under inspection. Clean the seat track and the exposed beam flange with the approved solvent and dry the area. Lay the channel lamp along the track so that the bottom of the open channel is lit for its full length. Do a detailed visual inspection along the full length of the track, giving attention to the channel bottom at each fastener hole and to the low points where fluid collects between the track pitches. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A METALLIC SCRAPER TO REMOVE CORROSION PRODUCT. USE THE NON-METALLIC PAD ONLY, BECAUSE A SCRATCH IN THE TRACK SURFACE WILL START A NEW ATTACK. Remove the loose corrosion product with the non-metallic pad and inspect again. Measure the depth of every pit with the depth gauge and record it against the track position. Use the inspection mirror to look into the channel where the seat leg slot narrows. WARNING: DO NOT ENTER THE BAY WITHOUT THE WORK PLATFORM IN POSITION. THE FLOOR BEAM UPPER FLANGE IS NOT A WALKWAY. Report any pit deeper than 0.25 mm, any attack that reaches a fastener hole, and any filiform run longer than 40 mm. Where the finding is inside the limits, blend it out, re-protect it and record the blend depth. Where it is outside, do not blend, and refer to the applicable repair scheme.
sections.close_out: Apply the corrosion preventive compound along the track and into the channel at the fastener line. Install the floor panels, the seats and the carpet. Record the measured depths and the blend depths against the bay identity, because the next inspection interval is set from them. Report any finding outside the limits to the operator engineering department before the aircraft is released.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The bays under the upper deck galleys and lavatories are inspected at every interval.

safety_precautions: Put the work platform across the floor beams before you go into the bay.
Use eye protection when you remove corrosion product.

tooling.description: Depth gauge, dial type, 0 to 3 mm

abstract: Repeat detailed inspection of the upper deck seat track and the beam flange beneath it in the bays under the galleys and the lavatories, written separately for the open channel and for the sealed and drained section.

sections.purpose: This task gives the repeat detailed inspection of the upper deck seat track and the floor beam upper flange in the bays under the galleys and the lavatories, and the criteria for reporting a corrosion finding.
sections.job_setup_note: The inspection needs the carpet up, the seats out of the bay and the floor panels lifted. Plan it with a cabin task that already opens the floor. Establish the track standard of the bay before you plan the lighting: on an open channel the attack is at the channel bottom and the channel lamp is laid along the run, and on a sealed and drained section there is no channel to light and the attack, where it occurs, is at the seal line and at the drain outlet. Have the depth gauge and the inspection mirror set available; filiform attack under a sealed track edge is not visible with a hand lamp alone.
sections.procedure: Remove the carpet, the seats and the floor panels from the bay under inspection. Establish the track standard of the bay and follow the branch for that standard. Clean the seat track and the exposed beam flange with the approved solvent and dry the area. On an open channel section, lay the channel lamp along the track and inspect the channel bottom at each fastener hole and at the low points between track pitches. On a sealed and drained section, inspect along the seal line for lifting or extrusion of the elastomer, at each splice, and at the drain outlet where the moulded channel meets the floor drain; the channel bottom is not accessible and is not part of this inspection. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A METALLIC SCRAPER TO REMOVE CORROSION PRODUCT. USE THE NON-METALLIC PAD ONLY, BECAUSE A SCRATCH IN THE TRACK SURFACE WILL START A NEW ATTACK. Remove the loose corrosion product with the non-metallic pad and inspect again. Measure the depth of every pit with the depth gauge and record it against the track position. Use the inspection mirror to look under the sealed track edge at each splice. WARNING: DO NOT ENTER THE BAY WITHOUT THE WORK PLATFORM IN POSITION. THE FLOOR BEAM UPPER FLANGE IS NOT A WALKWAY. Report any pit deeper than 0.25 mm, any attack that reaches a fastener hole, and any filiform run longer than 40 mm. On a drained section, also report any length of seal that has lifted and any drain outlet that does not pass water. Where the finding is inside the limits, blend it out, re-protect it and record the blend depth. Where it is outside, do not blend, and refer to the applicable repair scheme.
sections.close_out: Apply the corrosion preventive compound along the track and into the fastener line. On a drained section, prove the drain path with water before the floor panels go back. Install the floor panels, the seats and the carpet. Record the measured depths, the blend depths and the track standard of the bay against the bay identity, because the next inspection interval is set from them. Report any finding outside the limits to the operator engineering department before the aircraft is released.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft, in two branches by track standard. The open channel branch applies to bays pre the upper deck seat track rework and the drained section branch to bays that have taken it. The inspection may be cancelled on a deck once every bay is at the reworked standard.

safety_precautions: Put the work platform across the floor beams before you go into the bay.
Use eye protection when you remove corrosion product.

title: Upper Deck Seat Track in the Wet Bays — Detailed Corrosion Inspection

issue.reason: Description of the expected findings corrected for the titanium attachment fitting; the inspection interval is unchanged pending in-service evidence.

abstract: Repeat detailed inspection of the upper deck seat track and the beam flange beneath it in the bays under the galleys and the lavatories, where fluid ingress has produced filiform and pitting attack.

sections.purpose: This task gives the repeat detailed inspection of the upper deck seat track and the floor beam upper flange in the bays under the galleys and the lavatories, and the criteria for reporting a corrosion finding.
sections.job_setup_note: The inspection needs the carpet up, the seats out of the bay and the floor panels lifted. Plan it with a cabin task that already opens the floor. Establish the track standard and the attachment fitting standard of the bay before you plan the lighting: on an open channel the attack is at the channel bottom and the channel lamp is laid along the run, and on a sealed and drained section there is no channel to light and the attack, where it occurs, is at the seal line and at the drain outlet. On a bay at the titanium fitting standard the lug positions themselves are not a corrosion site and the white powdery product described for aluminium lugs will not be found there; what is looked for at those positions is disturbance of the isolation layer at the faying surface. Have the depth gauge and the inspection mirror set available; filiform attack under a sealed track edge is not visible with a hand lamp alone.
sections.procedure: Remove the carpet, the seats and the floor panels from the bay under inspection. Clean the seat track and the exposed beam flange with the approved solvent and dry the area. Do a detailed visual inspection along the full length of the track, giving attention to the fastener line and to the track edge where it meets the panel. CAUTION: DO NOT USE A METALLIC SCRAPER TO REMOVE CORROSION PRODUCT. USE THE NON-METALLIC PAD ONLY, BECAUSE A SCRATCH IN THE TRACK SURFACE WILL START A NEW ATTACK. Remove the loose corrosion product with the non-metallic pad and inspect again. Measure the depth of every pit with the depth gauge and record it against the track position. Use the inspection mirror to look under the sealed track edge at each splice. WARNING: DO NOT ENTER THE BAY WITHOUT THE WORK PLATFORM IN POSITION. THE FLOOR BEAM UPPER FLANGE IS NOT A WALKWAY. Report any pit deeper than 0.25 mm, any attack that reaches a fastener hole, and any filiform run longer than 40 mm. Where the finding is inside the limits, blend it out, re-protect it and record the blend depth. Where it is outside, do not blend, and refer to the applicable repair scheme.
sections.close_out: Apply the corrosion preventive compound along the track and into the fastener line. On a drained section, prove the drain path with water before the floor panels go back. Install the floor panels, the seats and the carpet. Record the measured depths, the blend depths, the track standard and the attachment fitting standard of the bay against the bay identity, because the next inspection interval is set from them. The interval is unchanged on a titanium fitting bay and stays under review until enough in-service returns exist to shorten or lengthen it. Report any finding outside the limits to the operator engineering department before the aircraft is released.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft, in two branches by track standard. The open channel branch applies to bays pre the upper deck seat track rework and the drained section branch to bays that have taken it. On bays at the titanium attachment fitting standard the interval is unchanged and only the expected findings differ. The inspection may be cancelled on a deck once every bay is at the reworked standard.

safety_precautions: Put the work platform across the floor beams before you go into the bay.
Use eye protection when you remove corrosion product.
